A 'Soft Room' is the name for a place in a police station or courthouse where children and mentally feeble adults stay and play with toys and coloring books while the adults in their lives move around outside doing things that might confuse or frighten the children if they saw it. The room allows the children to feel safe and secure while shielding them from the harsher aspects of life that adults learn to adapt to as they mature.

I get it. People have a high opinion of Voat and want it to be a center of intellectual discourse. And in a lot of ways, it is. One of those ways is that people can have opinions and be open about them without someone censoring them. Being downvoted is not being censored, it is having people doubt the quality of your opinion, which is what the button is for - bad presentation of poor quality. They think you're view is shit and you haven't presented an argument very well, or your link is shit and not worth the time it takes to click it (or it's behind a paywall - get it together people, this is not okay). It is an acceptable use of the button -even if you don't agree. 'One man's trash is another man's treasure.' Your treasure is trash - go back and try again. Don't whine and cry about how good your opinion is, form a better argument and come back later.

The people making this argument aren't talking about censorship, they're saying they don't want anyone to disagree with them. See, the great thing about the internet is anonymity - lots of people get on here and run their fingers about shit they wouldn't dare talk about within punching range of another human being. The terrible thing about the internet is *anonymity *- no one gives two shits about you, and if you have an unpopular opinion and can't get it across in a civil way that people can understand no one is going to want to read it. And they can use whatever means they see fit to make sure you understand that - free-will and all that stuff. I've seen so many downvoted posts along the lines of: ''But I want to go to a gun-centered sub-verse and tell them all that guns kill more people than cancer, car accidents, and AIDS combined! Intellectual discourse means thinking out a strategy and forming a plan of attack. You want to make a good point? Start with reliable sources. The simple act of looking shit up might make your argument stronger - or let it crumble in your head where it should have stayed in the first place.
